concern_details.detail: main data entities stored and their relationships
concern_details.why: All seven persistence-unit entities (persistence.xml:14-20) plus the two embeddables are drawn with table names, ids, key columns, and associations with multiplicities that match the JPA mappings (e.g. Report.java:87-112, Notification.java:48-54).

concern_details.detail: information persisted throughout the lifecycle of a report
concern_details.why: Shows that the state is stored only as Report.currentStatusName plus citizenEditable (ReportStatus is transient, Report.java:69-82), that each transition appends a StatusUpdate with date, new status and operator (Report.java:367-383), that operators add internal notes, and that notifications record the notified status. The allowed status string values are not listed (see minor finding).

concern_details.detail: how users, reports, locations, categories, states, state changes, internal notes and notifications are related
concern_details.why: Every named concept is an element: Report embeds Location, uses the ReportCategory enum, has a transient ReportStatus, composes StatusUpdate and InternalNote, references Citizen (1) and MunicipalOperator (0..1). Notification references Report and Citizen. StatusUpdate and InternalNote reference the operator.

concern_details.detail: which parts of the application depend on the persisted information
concern_details.why: Shows the dependency chain Boundary -> Control -> ReportService/UserService -> PersistenceService (JPA), and which entities each service reads or writes.

level_why: For a detailed data-model view, the entities show attributes with types, ids, the unique constraint, the discriminator, embeddables and multiplicities. Application dependents are grouped by package, which fits a persistence focus and does not bury the entity model. Physical details such as column lengths and nullability are left out, which is acceptable here.

findings.claim: The view says only the state name is stored, but it does not list the actual values written to reports.current_status and status_updates.new_status ('submitted', 'assigned', 'in_progress', 'resolved'). It names the classes Submitted, Assigned and so on instead. A DB engineer changing the column needs the stored literals.
findings.fix: Add the four stored string values to the ReportStatus note (or to currentStatusName/newStatus).

findings.claim: ReportService also reads users (it loads User/Citizen when creating a report, and MunicipalOperator when assigning or updating) and queries notifications by report. The view shows only 'creates' toward Notification and no edge toward the user entities.
findings.fix: Relabel rs ..> notif as 'creates, reads' and add rs ..> user 'finds'.

findings.claim: StatusUpdate and InternalNote each hold a mandatory back-reference to Report (report_id NOT NULL). The composition edges carry this implicitly, but the foreign-key columns and the operator FK nullability (operator_id nullable on reports, NOT NULL on status_updates/internal_notes) are not visible.
findings.fix: Optionally annotate the association ends with the FK column names (report_id, operator_id, citizen_id).

findings.claim: The Control and Boundary packages are drawn as classes (class symbols with a '(10 controllers)' label) rather than as UML packages.
findings.fix: Draw ctl and gui with UML package notation, or mark them as package-level groupings.

findings.claim: Attribute names are the Java field names, not the column names, and some differ: InternalNote.dateEntry is column created_date, and Report.dateReport is report_date. For a database engineer this can mislead when matching the diagram to the schema.
findings.fix: Show column names where they differ from field names, e.g. 'dateEntry : Date «created_date»'.
